summary: The remediation closed several prior findings, but trusted preparation and private plan sealing remain bypassable at the immutable audited HEAD.
blocking_findings: ID: P2-RB-V2-001. Severity: critical. Title: Trusted preparation does not bind normalized document facts. Evidence: packages/backend/src/modules/finance-operations/controlled-imports.ts:335-358 compares scope, source identity, digest, and evidence reference. It never compares the envelope document with preparation.packet.facts. Lines 370-471 then normalize the caller envelope. A safe runtime probe used a genuine preparation with source value 100.00 and an envelope value 999.00. The function returned amountMinor 99900. Impact: A caller can replace owner-attested financial facts while retaining genuine preparation branding. Recommendation: Derive normalized facts from the validated packet, or bind the exact document to verified evidence.

ID: P2-RB-V2-002. Severity: critical. Title: Symbol checks and deep freezing do not provide private capability sealing. Evidence: packages/backend/src/modules/finance-operations/contracts.ts:454-466 exports isHistoricalPrivateEvidencePreparation and uses Reflect.get with a module-local symbol. A Proxy can return true for every symbol and supply caller data. The probe produced status ready from this forged preparation. packages/backend/src/modules/finance-operations/controlled-imports.ts:603-609 also accepts any deeply frozen caller-built plan as an alternative to the private symbol. The probe reached the repository and returned accepted. Impact: Callers can forge trusted preparations and acceptance plans. Recommendation: Use module-private WeakSet or WeakMap identity checks. Remove the deep-freeze bypass. Do not export a trust predicate that reads attacker-controlled objects.

ID: P2-RB-V2-003. Severity: high. Title: Repository results cross the command boundary without runtime validation. Evidence: packages/backend/src/modules/finance-operations/controlled-imports.ts:641-651 clones and returns the repository value directly. A safe probe returned an accepted result with secret: leak, and the command exposed that field. Impact: A faulty adapter can return unknown fields or malformed status data. Recommendation: Parse the repository result with a strict discriminated union before return.
nonblocking_findings: ID: P2-RB-V2-004. Severity: low. Title: Authorization dependency failures do not create failed audit events. Evidence: packages/backend/src/modules/finance-operations/controlled-imports.ts:611-619 parses the authorization result outside the repository try block. A throw or malformed result exits before a failed event. Impact: The audit trail omits authorization infrastructure failures. Recommendation: Append a sanitized failed event when authorization evaluation fails.

ID: P2-RB-V2-005. Severity: low. Title: Decimal input has no digit limit. Evidence: packages/backend/src/modules/finance-operations/controlled-imports.ts:31-33 and 285-297 accept an unbounded decimal string before BigInt conversion. Impact: A large value can consume excessive CPU and memory. Recommendation: Set an explicit decimal digit limit.

test_strategy_violations: The trusted preparation tests bind metadata, but they do not bind normalized document facts to packet facts or immutable evidence bytes.
The caller-plan test uses a mutable object. It does not refute the documented deep-freeze fallback.
The security suite does not test a Proxy that returns true for unknown symbols.
The security suite does not test strict repository result parsing.
live_contract_violations: Owner-attested packet facts can differ from the normalized financial facts.
A Proxy can forge the trusted preparation predicate.
A deeply frozen caller-built plan can reach atomic repository acceptance.
Unknown repository result fields can cross the public command boundary.
prod_wiring_violations: The public Finance barrel exports prepareControlledImportBatch, acceptControlledImportBatch, and isHistoricalPrivateEvidencePreparation.
The acceptance command has a deep-freeze alternative to its private capability.
The normalization command consumes caller document facts instead of deriving them from the trusted preparation.
